## Stage 1 — Sold

- [ ] Proposal accepted — option [A/B/C]
- [ ] Contract signed by both parties
- [ ] **Deposit received and cleared**
- [ ] Project added to the schedule
- [ ] Start and launch dates confirmed in writing

> Nothing below starts until the deposit clears. This is the discipline that
> protects every project after it.

## Stage 2 — Kickoff (week 1)

- [ ] Welcome guide sent
- [ ] Kickoff call held
- [ ] Approver confirmed in writing: ______________
- [ ] Branding questionnaire sent → returned ☐
- [ ] Technical questionnaire sent → returned ☐
- [ ] Content planner sent
- [ ] Asset checklist sent
- [ ] Shared folder created and shared: [LINK]
- [ ] Content deadline agreed: [DATE]

## Stage 3 — Requirements

- [ ] Requirements document drafted
- [ ] Sent for review with the sign-off form
- [ ] Corrections received and applied
- [ ] **Requirements signed** — this is the scope of record
- [ ] Version filed: v[1.0], [DATE]

> Do not start design without this. It's the thing you point at every time
> scope drifts.

- [ ] Environment set up
- [ ] Templates built

- [ ] **Full site presented** — [DATE]

- [ ] Portfolio updated

---

## Weekly rhythm

Every Friday, ten minutes:

- [ ] Progress note sent to the client — even if it's "on track, nothing
      needed from you"
- [ ] Content chase updated
- [ ] Schedule still realistic?
- [ ] Anything that should be a change order but isn't yet?
- [ ] Invoices due?

> The Friday note is disproportionately valuable. Silence makes clients
> anxious, and anxious clients invent scope.
